summary: A line chart that compares a main series with one or more reference series over time, such as this year against last year. A big number above it counts up to the latest value, and a readout follows the pointer to show the value at each point. In an agent product it suits a usage or growth metric on a dashboard.
use: When you want to show a metric's trend over time next to the same period before.
When the latest value matters most and should be the headline.
When people need to read exact values by hovering, without a full analytics tool.
features: The first entry in `series` draws as a solid line with a soft fill; the others draw dashed for comparison.
The lines draw in from the left while the headline number counts up to the last value.
Moving the pointer shows a guide line, dots on each series and a readout with the value, the point's name from `points`, and, with `compareLabel`, the percent change between the first two series.
Legend buttons toggle each series on and off; one series always stays on.
`range` fixes the bottom and top values, `axis` sets the labels along the bottom, and `format` and `unit` control how values read.
a11y: Each legend button uses aria-pressed to show whether its series is visible.
The SVG drawing is aria-hidden, so the headline number and legend are what a screen reader gets.
The count-up of the headline number finishes at once when the user prefers reduced motion.

faq.q: How do I show "+69% vs last year" in the readout?
faq.a: Pass `compareLabel`, like "vs last year". The readout then adds the percent change of the first series against the second at the hovered point, as long as both are visible.

faq.q: Can I plot more than two series?
faq.a: Yes. `series` takes any number; the first is the solid main line and the rest are dashed. The percent comparison only uses the first two.

faq.q: How do I keep the y-axis from starting near the lowest value?
faq.a: Pass `range` as [bottom, top]. Without it, the chart uses the data's range with a little room above and below.

faq.q: Can I control which series are visible?
faq.a: Yes. Pass `visible` with the keys to show and handle `onVisibleChange`, or use `defaultVisible` and let the legend manage it.
